flag_description: Severe or heavy vaginal bleeding reported — possible placenta previa, abruption, or postpartum haemorrhage. Immediate emergency referral required.
recommended_asha_action: Do NOT attempt home management. Call 108 immediately. Keep patient lying flat, do not give anything by mouth, monitor pulse. Accompany patient to nearest FRU/hospital.
source: WHO Recommendations on Antenatal Care for a Positive Pregnancy Experience (2016)

flag_description: Visual disturbance in pregnancy or the postpartum period is a cardinal sign of severe pre-eclampsia and may precede eclampsia. Postpartum pre-eclampsia can present up to 6 weeks after delivery.
recommended_asha_action: Measure blood pressure immediately. If ≥140/90 mmHg, or if headache or epigastric pain co-occur, call 108 and refer to FRU without delay. Do not wait for the next scheduled visit.
source: WHO Recommendations on Antenatal Care for a Positive Pregnancy Experience (2016)

flag_description: Breathlessness may indicate severe anaemia, cardiac decompensation, pulmonary oedema or, postpartum, pulmonary embolism.
recommended_asha_action: Sit the patient upright. Check for pallor and swelling. Call 108 for immediate transport to FRU. Do not allow the patient to walk to the facility.
source: WHO Recommendations on Antenatal Care for a Positive Pregnancy Experience (2016)

flag_description: Severe abdominal pain may indicate placental abruption, uterine rupture, ectopic pregnancy or, postpartum, uterine infection.
recommended_asha_action: Do not give painkillers or home remedies. Call 108 immediately and refer to FRU. Note the time the pain began and whether bleeding accompanies it.
source: WHO Recommendations on Antenatal Care for a Positive Pregnancy Experience (2016)

flag_description: Convulsions in pregnancy or within 6 weeks of delivery indicate eclampsia until proven otherwise. This is an immediately life-threatening obstetric emergency.
recommended_asha_action: Turn the patient onto her left side. Do not put anything in her mouth. Protect her from injury. Call 108 immediately. This is a life-threatening emergency — accompany her to the FRU.
source: WHO Recommendations on Antenatal Care for a Positive Pregnancy Experience (2016)

flag_description: Reduced or absent fetal movement after 28 weeks is a leading warning sign of fetal compromise and precedes a significant share of stillbirths. It must never be dismissed as normal late-pregnancy quietening.
recommended_asha_action: Ask the mother to lie on her left side and count movements for two hours. Fewer than 10 movements, or any report of complete absence, requires same-day referral to a facility with foetal heart monitoring. Do not wait for the next ANC visit.
source: Government of India, Guidelines for Antenatal Care and Skilled Attendance at Birth (MoHFW)

flag_description: Rupture of membranes before labour carries a high risk of ascending infection and cord prolapse. Before 37 weeks it is preterm prelabour rupture and requires urgent facility care.
recommended_asha_action: Do NOT perform any vaginal examination. Note the time of rupture and the colour and smell of the fluid (green or foul-smelling is an emergency). Arrange immediate transport to a delivery facility.
source: Government of India, Guidelines for Antenatal Care and Skilled Attendance at Birth (MoHFW)

flag_description: High fever in pregnancy or the postpartum period suggests serious infection — chorioamnionitis, puerperal sepsis, malaria or severe UTI. Puerperal sepsis is a leading direct cause of maternal death in India.
recommended_asha_action: Measure temperature. If ≥38°C (100.4°F), or fever with foul-smelling discharge, abdominal tenderness or rapid pulse, refer to PHC/FRU the same day. Start no antibiotics at home; encourage fluids during transport.
source: Government of India, Home Based Newborn Care (HBNC) Operational Guidelines, MoHFW

flag_description: A severe or persistent headache unrelieved by rest is a cardinal pre-eclampsia sign, particularly alongside visual disturbance, epigastric pain or oedema. Postpartum onset is equally significant.
recommended_asha_action: Measure blood pressure immediately. If ≥140/90 mmHg, test urine for albumin at the sub-centre and refer the same day. If ≥160/110 mmHg or accompanied by visual symptoms, call 108.
source: WHO Recommendations on Antenatal Care for a Positive Pregnancy Experience (2016)

flag_description: Marked pallor of the palms, conjunctiva or tongue suggests severe anaemia (Hb <7 g/dL), which sharply raises the risk of haemorrhagic death at delivery and of cardiac failure.
recommended_asha_action: Check palms, conjunctiva and tongue against the anaemia card. Arrange haemoglobin testing at the PHC within 48 hours. Severe pallor with breathlessness requires same-day referral, not IFA tablets alone.
source: Anemia Mukt Bharat, Government of India Operational Guidelines

flag_description: Foul-smelling lochia is the defining sign of puerperal sepsis, a leading direct cause of maternal death in India. It typically appears between days 2 and 10 after delivery.
recommended_asha_action: Measure temperature and pulse and palpate for uterine tenderness. Refer to FRU the same day for IV antibiotics. Do not treat with home remedies or delay to the next HBNC visit.
source: Government of India, Home Based Newborn Care (HBNC) Operational Guidelines, MoHFW

symptom: Calf Pain or One-Sided Leg Swelling
flag_description: Unilateral calf pain or swelling after delivery suggests deep vein thrombosis, which can progress to fatal pulmonary embolism. Bilateral swelling is a different sign and is less specific.
recommended_asha_action: Do not massage the leg — massage can dislodge a clot. Keep the patient still and refer to an FRU the same day. If breathlessness or chest pain is also present, call 108 immediately.
source: WHO Recommendations on Postnatal Care of the Mother and Newborn (2013)

flag_description: Expressed thoughts of self-harm, harm to the infant, or signs of postpartum psychosis constitute a psychiatric emergency. Suicide is among the leading causes of maternal death in the year after childbirth.
recommended_asha_action: Do not leave the mother alone with the infant. Inform a responsible family member immediately and arrange same-day referral to the medical officer. Report the exact words used — do not paraphrase or soften them.
source: WHO Recommendations on Postnatal Care of the Mother and Newborn (2013)

flag_description: HBNC newborn danger signs — poor feeding, hypothermia, lethargy, fast breathing, chest indrawing, jaundice or umbilical infection — indicate possible neonatal sepsis, which progresses within hours.
recommended_asha_action: Keep the baby warm with skin-to-skin contact during transport. Do not bathe the baby. Refer to the nearest SNCU/NBSU immediately — neonatal sepsis progresses within hours, not days.
source: Government of India, Home Based Newborn Care (HBNC) Operational Guidelines, MoHFW
